title: Travel Protection Plans: Rating Manual, the Difference a Re-Rating Raises
content:
## 1. The difference

1.1 Where a declared particular of a Travel Protection Plans certificate has been corrected, the premium is re-rated and the difference between the premium the certificate now calls for and the premium already charged is raised as its own line.

## 2. The premium the certificate now calls for

2.1 It is the certificate's declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate, followed by the loadings that attach to it and by the uplift the party named carries.

2.2 The loadings that attach add nothing.

2.3 The uplift the party named carries is the whole of the premium and no more, 100 per cent of it.

## 3. The premium already charged

3.1 It is the figure the certificate records as premium paid.

## 4. Apportionment and evidence

4.1 The difference is then apportioned over the days of cover remaining from the day the correction takes effect out of the days of cover bought, and it is taken at the share the evidence behind the correction carries.

4.2 The day the correction takes effect is the first day of the journey insured.

4.3 The days of cover bought are counted from the first day of the journey insured to its last day, both days counted, and the days of cover remaining are counted from the day the correction takes effect to the last day of the journey insured, both days counted; the days of cover remaining never fall below nothing.

4.4 The share the evidence behind the correction carries is 60 per cent.

4.5 The difference so apportioned is rounded to two decimal places.

## 5. The quantity defined in order

The declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate is established first; what the loadings that attach add is applied to it, and then the uplift the party named carries, giving the premium the certificate now calls for. The premium already charged is subtracted from that figure, giving the difference. The difference is then multiplied by the days of cover remaining and divided by the days of cover bought, and the result is taken at the share the evidence behind the correction carries. The rounding to two decimal places is done last, on the figure that results.

## 6. Worked to a figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a certificate declaring a trip cost of 9000.00 USD on a plan whose base premium rate is 5 per cent, recording 380.00 USD as premium paid, on a journey whose first day is the 1st of a month and whose last day is the 20th of that month.

- The declared trip cost at the plan's base premium rate is 5 per cent of 9000.00 USD, which is 450.00 USD.
- The loadings that attach add nothing, so the figure stands at 450.00 USD.
- The uplift the party named carries is 100 per cent of it, so the premium the certificate now calls for is 450.00 USD.
- The premium already charged is the figure the certificate records as premium paid, 380.00 USD, so the difference is 70.00 USD.
- The day the correction takes effect is the first day of the journey insured, the 1st. The days of cover bought are the 1st to the 20th, both counted, which is 20 days; the days of cover remaining are the 1st to the 20th, both counted, which is also 20 days.
- The difference apportioned over 20 days out of 20 days is 70.00 USD.
- At the share the evidence behind the correction carries, 60 per cent, that is 42.00 USD.

The difference so apportioned, rounded to two decimal places, is 42.00 USD, and that is the amount of the adjustment line.
